transcript.text: bosch washer FD 9409 not draining. ive cleaned the filter already. what part do i need?

Please run a drain or spin-only programme on your Bosch washing machine. While it attempts to pump out, listen near the bottom front of the appliance. If any water has reached the plug or socket, do not touch it; tell me straight away instead. Also, the door will stay locked until the water has gone, so please do not try to force it open. Does the water pump away, and can you hear the pump humming or is it silent?
water doesn't pump away, pump hums but nothing moves. no burning smell. is it the pump then?

Thanks for those details about the pump humming and water remaining. Please switch off and unplug the machine first. Keep the filter out and do not remove any panels. Using only a torch and your finger, shine into the filter opening and gently turn the small plastic impeller vanes. Do not use tools inside the housing. The app shows a video to help you with this step. Does it turn freely, was anything caught in it, is it jammed, or do the vanes look broken?
[Helpful to see: video "How to unblock the pump / drain filter" — Typical procedure for clearing a blocked pump filter and drain pump — switch the machine off and drain the water first. Access can vary by model.]
ok did that. impeller turns but feels a bit stiff and gritty in places. nothing big stuck in there. also E18 came up on the display when it stalled.

I have noted the E18 code on your Bosch FD9409 display; this step is the right place to start regardless of that reading. Before checking anything, please switch the machine off and unplug it first. The appliance is heavy and may still hold water, so ease it forward carefully, ideally with help. Put towels down and have a shallow tray or baking dish ready, as several litres of water can come out. Do not disconnect the hose while there is still water in the machine. Next, check the drain hose at the back for kinks or crushing, and inspect where it enters the standpipe or sink waste. Was the hose clear, did you find and clear a kink or blockage, or is there one you can't clear?
hose behind looks OK, no kinks. I also took it off at the sink and blew through it, it's clear. sink drains fine too. so is it the pump?

[Heading: Blocked pump filter]
Thank you for confirming that the drain hose is clear. Based on what we have checked so far, the most likely cause of the issue is a blockage in the pump filter. An appliance engineer is the best next step to confirm this and carry out any necessary repairs.
